fieldValues.title: RFC-017 Change E: Soft size-warning conformance
fieldValues.proposed_change: When an `attachment_policy` is present, an implementation MAY enforce its limits as hard rejections. If it does not enforce them as hard limits, it MUST surface violations as non-blocking warning diagnostics at `srs repo validate` time: when a source document content file exceeds `max_per_file_bytes` or `max_doc_bytes`; when aggregate source-document bytes exceed `max_total_bytes`; when an attached file's MIME type is not listed in `allowed_mime_types`. Non-blocking diagnostics MUST NOT prevent record storage or repository export. Whether to emit a warning at write time (e.g. `srs source import`) is implementation-defined; conformance is required at validate time. Hard caps are deferred to a future extension.
fieldValues.rationale: Hard size caps at the spec level would set arbitrary limits that break legitimate use cases (e.g., video-heavy documentary repositories). Soft warnings surfaced as diagnostics give operators visibility without blocking valid workflows; the application layer or a future hard-cap extension can enforce stricter limits.
